title: Match a deep link to a route file
prompt:
Implement `matchRoute(url, routes)` the way Expo Router picks a screen for a deep link. `routes` are file paths without `.tsx` (see `ROUTES`). Return `{ route, params }` for the best match, or `null`.

- Groups such as `(tabs)` and a final `index` add no URL segment.
- `[id]` matches exactly one segment and adds it to `params` as a string.
- `[...path]` matches **one or more** remaining segments and adds them as an array.
- When several routes match, prefer static segments over `[dynamic]` ones, and `[dynamic]` over `[...catchAll]`, comparing from the first segment.
- Ignore a trailing slash; add query-string values (`?units=mi`) to `params`.
hints: Turn each route into its URL segments first: drop `(group)` segments and a trailing `index`. Split the URL path with `.split('/').filter(Boolean)`.
Walk the route's segments alongside the URL's. A literal must equal the URL segment; `[x]` captures it; `[...x]` captures `parts.slice(i)` and ends the match. Afterwards, the lengths must line up.
To rank, build a string per match with one digit per segment (3 static, 2 dynamic, 1 catch-all) and keep the match with the largest string. `new URLSearchParams(query)` iterates the query pairs.
explanation: The solution normalizes each route file into URL segments, tries to match it segment by segment while collecting params, and scores each segment so that more specific routes win: comparing the score strings ranks static before dynamic before catch-all from left to right. That's why `/hikes/new` reaches `hikes/new.tsx` while `/hikes/42` falls through to `hikes/[id].tsx`, and why the screen must still validate `id`: the matcher accepts any segment at all.

checks.groups-index: Groups and index files add no URL segment
checks.dynamic: Dynamic segments match and become string params
checks.static-wins: A static route beats a dynamic one
checks.catch-all: Catch-all routes collect the remaining segments as an array
checks.query-slash: Query strings become params and trailing slashes are ignored
checks.no-match: Unknown or too-long paths return null
